body:
### Summary

With `UV_GCS_ENDPOINT_URL` pointing at Google Artifact Registry and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` set to a workload identity federation (`external_account`) config, `uv sync` failed with `403 Forbidden` when downloading wheels. The cause was only visible with `RUST_LOG=reqsign_core=debug`: reqsign-google couldn't parse the credential file (`data did not match any variant of untagged enum Source`, because `credential_source.format` was missing; upstream issue: https://github.com/apache/reqsign/issues/909). It then fell back to the GCE metadata server and signed requests as the node's default service account.

At default verbosity uv gives no hint that the configured credentials were ignored, and even `-v` doesn't show reqsign's warning. Two things would have made this much easier to diagnose:
- Fail, or at least warn, when `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is set but can't be loaded, instead of quietly using another identity. Google's client libraries raise in this case.
- Include reqsign's credential-loading warnings in uv's `-v` output.

Workaround: add `"format": {"type": "text"}` to `credential_source`.

### Platform

Linux x86_64 (Docker, debian:trixie, on GKE-based CI runners)

### Version

uv 0.12.23 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl)

### Python version

3.11
title: gcs-endpoint: unparseable GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS silently falls back to VM metadata identity
